Subject: Recap & Test Plan — Compatibility + Differentiators

Hi Alyssa / Tom,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great discussion and helpful context about BrightLayer's inference targets (short responses, aggressive p95 latency goals, and cost sensitivity on bulk embedding jobs). I wanted to summarize where we landed and propose a lightweight, hands-on test plan to validate OpenAI-compatibility and hyperscaler comparisons.

Quick recap (what you told us):
- Primary workload: customer-facing microcopy and 1–2k embedding batches/day.
- Requirements: p95 < 150ms for text-gen L1 flows; <100ms for smaller token responses is a stretch target.
- Constraints: existing rely-on-OpenAI SDKs and tooling; procurement favors predictable unit costs and SSO/KMS readiness.

Where Redwood helps (differentiators to validate):
- Drop-in OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDK adapters: same auth + similar request shapes to minimize code churn.
- Deterministic latency controls: reserved capacity + policy routing for stable p95s across peak windows.
- Cost levers: KV/prefix caching + batching recommendations we can auto-suggest per workload.
- Graceful fallbacks: automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants if a model tier is out of capacity.

Proposed hands-on test plan (two-week lightweight matrix):
1) OpenAI-compat sanity test (Day 1)
   - Run sample prompts through Redwood OpenAI-compatible endpoint (no code changes)
   - Verify response shape, streaming behavior, and function-calling parity (if used)
2) SDK swap (Day 2–3)
   - Try our SDK adapter (npm install @redwood/inference) + one-line replacement example (we'll provide snippet)
   - Validate token accounting and error codes match your expectations
3) Latency & cost matrix (Days 3–7)
   - 1000 synthetic requests at your typical token mix vs. equivalent tests on Hyperscaler A and Hyperscaler B
   - Metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, cost-per-1000-tokens
4) Prompt-diff checks (concurrent)
   - Tokenization differences, stop-sequence behavior, streaming chunk sizes, and recommended prompt edits if we detect tokenization drift
5) Security touchpoints (ongoing)
   - We'll send SOC2 artefacts and KMS integration checklist.

Deliverables we'll provide:
- interop-checklist.xlsx (test matrix + sample prompts)
- sample-sdk-patch.diff (tiny code adaptor you can apply)
- side-by-side results template (CSV) and a basic Grafana dashboard template

Next steps / asks for BrightLayer:
- Confirm two engineers to run tests and a day/time for a short handoff call (30m) this week.
- Share a small set of representative prompts and a sample embedding batch (anonymized) we can use for the tests.

I'll follow up with the SDK snippet and the checklist attachment.

Best,

Thanks Alyssa — great. A couple of technical clarifications and an explicit test matrix so your engineers can run these without surprises.

Test matrix (concrete):
- Sanity (0): curl vs OpenAI-compat endpoint
  - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/compat/completions 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","prompt":"Say hello","max_tokens":16}'
  - Validate: status codes (200/4xx/5xx), response fields ('id','choices','usage'), and streaming chunk headers if used

- SDK swap (1): Node sample
  - npm i @redwood/inference@latest
  - const rwd = require('@redwood/inference');
  - const client = new rwd.Client({ apiKey: process.env.RWD_KEY, compat: true });
  - client.completions.create({ model: 'redwood-1-small', prompt, max_tokens: 16 })
  - Look for matching error shapes and retryable vs non-retryable error codes

- Latency matrix (2): run 1k warm + 1k measured requests for your small-response flow against:
  - Redwood (Hosted) — reserved pool
  - Hyperscaler A (their managed endpoint)
  - Hyperscaler B (managed endpoint)
  - Capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cold-start counts. We'll provide a small JMeter script if useful.

Prompt-diff checklist (things to watch):
- Subtle tokenization shifts (esp. punctuation and special tokens) — we provide a tokenizer diff tool in the interop-checklist.xlsx
- Stop-sequence handling: ensure both systems behave identically with multiple stops and streaming interrupts
- Function-calling / structured outputs: confirm key ordering and key-name preservation in JSON outputs

Procurement / SOW baseline for finance:
- I'll put together a short ballpark for a 6-month pilot: reserved 4x GPU capacity (estimated) + usage overage tiers. Nikhil — can you send a quick pilot pricing outline (monthly commit, unit price per 1M tokens)? We can ship to BrightLayer's procurement team.

I'll attach small helper scripts and the JMeter scenario in the checklist. If you want, we can run a short live test with you on Thursday during the handoff and produce preliminary charts same-day.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
